newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia 1997 tin output seen down - Negara.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia 1997 tin output seen down - Negara.

text.p: Malaysia's tin production is expected to fall again this year as miners adhere to the "national depletion policy" on sustainable mining, Bank Negara Malaysia said on Friday in its 1996 annual report.
The central bank did not give estimates for the reduced output.
Production of tin-in-concentrates fell in 1996 for the seventh consecutive year, by 19.2 percent to 5.17 million tonnes against 6.40 million in 1995, the report said.
The reason for the lower ouput was the closure of seven tin mines in 1996, which left only 35 active, it said.
"Despite this, Malaysia maintained its position as the world's seventh largest producer of tin," the report said.
Imports of tin-in-concentrates rose a sharp 54.7 percent to 49,821 tonnes. These came mainly from Peru, Australia, Portugal, South Africa and Bolivia.
Total domestic consumption fell 9.3 percent to 5,800 tonnes, primarily on account of lower demand from the solder and tin plate industries.
